title: Scoped token migration, rotation automation, and operator toolkit
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: We currently have a mix of long-lived org- and service-level API keys with inconsistent naming and no enforced expiry. This increases blast radius for leaked keys and complicates audit and automated rotation. Goal: Replace legacy keys with per-scope short-lived tokens (ephemeral where possible), deploy automated rotation and naming conventions, and provide operators with a safe migration and rollback toolkit. Non-goals: Replacing user OAuth flows or changing SSO provider configuration in this ticket. We will not encrypt token payloads in a custom format — we will use existing KMS/HSM integrations.
acceptance_criteria: New token naming standard published and validated by 3 teams
Rotation automation deployed for platform service account tokens with zero downtime in canary region
All legacy org-level keys listed in inventory; plan to retire 80% of them by end of migration window
Audit logs surface token_id, issuer, scope, rotation_event_id, and previous_key_hash for every rotate/issue event
RBAC v2 maps token scopes to role bindings; at least two internal services enforce scope checks using new middleware
Operator CLI (tokenctl) supports rotate, stage, rollback and shows dependent services for a token
technical_notes: Core pieces: 1) Token issuer service extension to support per-scope short-lived JWTs and opaque tokens with KMS-wrapped secrets; 2) Rotation controller that atomically stages new credentials, updates downstream credential mounts (K8s secret or Vault), announces change to a service registry, and then retires the old token after health checks pass; 3) Audit-forwarding changes to include structured fields for token lifecycle events; 4) Token naming scheme: <org>-<env>-<surface>-<short-hash>-<issued-at-YYYYMMDD> (max 64 chars). Implementation details include deterministic secondary index for token_id -> service bindings, and adding token_age histogram to metrics. Avoid requiring callers to handle token refresh; provide sidecar or credential proxy for services that can't be changed immediately.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): Publish design and name standard; create inventory of high-risk long-lived keys
Phase 2 (Week 2-3): Implement rotation controller and operator CLI; add audit fields to log pipeline; deploy in staging
Phase 3 (Week 4): Canary rotation for non-critical infra services in us-west-2; verify zero downtime and alerting
Phase 4 (Week 5-8): Gradual migration of customer-facing services and platform databases; run token expiry enforcement in monitor-only mode first
Phase 5 (Week 9): Enforce expiry and revoke legacy keys; run post-mortem and follow-up bug fixes
migration_steps: Run discovery job to enumerate keys across config stores, vaults, and environment variables; output CSV with owners and usage frequency
Classify keys by criticality and ability to accept short-lived creds; tag teams for manual intervention where required
For each service: deploy credential-proxy sidecar (if service cannot be updated) to translate new per-scope tokens into existing internal credential format
Schedule automated rotations during low-traffic windows; use operator CLI to stage and monitor each rotation
Communicate deprecation timeline to teams and create migration tickets for blocked services
testing_plan: Unit tests for issuer, rotation controller, and audit payload generation
Integration tests that simulate staged key swap with health-check gating and rollback path
Chaos test: simulate credential store latency and KMS HSM unavailability during rotation
Load-test: measure token issuance QPS and latency under expected peak with caching enabled
Security test: verification that revoked tokens fail auth and that token age metrics are accurate
monitoring_and_alerts: Alerts: spike in failed auths post-rotation, rotation controller errors > 1/min, degradation in KMS latency
Dashboards: per-team token age distribution, number of legacy keys remaining, rotation success rate
SLO: 99.9% successful rotations without client-visible auth failures within canary window
stakeholders: Leah Park - PM for RBAC v2
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Rotation causes auth failures in services that read keys from env; Mitigation: credential-proxy sidecar and staged rollout
Risk: Audit pipeline misses fields due to schema drift; Mitigation: schema validation and pipeline contract tests
Risk: KMS quota limits during mass rotation; Mitigation: stagger rotations and use local caching with attenuation TTL
Risk: Teams delay migration causing extended legacy key exposure; Mitigation: send automated reminders and block new legacy key creation via policy
notes: This ticket will coordinate closely with the RBAC v2 rollout (mapping scopes to roles) and SSO/SAML team for issuer identities. The operator CLI ('tokenctl') should be built to be idempotent and produce an audit event for each action. Follow-on work: automated cross-account token audit and monthly leakage scans.
follow_up_actions: Create training doc and run two internal workshops for platform and infra teams
Add token expiry enforcement to account creation guardrails
Schedule a security audit one month after full enforcement
